2022_15_9_f_troy_2022_bond_app_6_16_22.paragraph: Michigan Department of Treasury Form 3881, an Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, filed by Troy School District for a November 8, 2022 election and certified by the Board of Education on June 21, 2022. The ballot proposition seeks authority to borrow not to exceed $555,000,000 in general obligation unlimited tax bonds, issued in three series of $167,000,000, $188,000,000 and $200,000,000, for remodeling, a replacement middle school, additions, instructional technology, sites and school buses. Annual debt millage is expected to be at or below 6.10 mills, a 2 mill increase over the 4.10 mills of debt millage levied in 2022.

## Filing and authority

Michigan Department of Treasury Form 3881 (Rev. 09-19), Application for Preliminary Qualification of Bonds, School Bond Qualification and Loan Program, issued under Public Act 92 of 2005. Application No. 63-150-4-K12-22-01; election date November 8, 2022. Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, MI 48098, district code 63-150; Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky. The Board certificate recites action at a regular meeting on the 21st day of June 2022 under the Open Meetings Act (Act 276 of 1976), signed by Secretary Gary Hauff, with Treasurer Rick West and Superintendent Machesky.

Team: bond counsel Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. (Detroit); financial consultant PFM Financial Advisors LLC, Ann Arbor, prepared by Paul Stauder; architect TMP Architecture, Bloomfield Hills (John J Castellana, FAIA, license 21298); construction manager Barton Malow Builders, Southfield.

## Ballot language

School Improvement Bond Proposition asking whether the district shall borrow not to exceed Five Hundred Fifty-Five Million Dollars ($555,000,000) in one or more series for remodeling and equipping buildings, athletic fields and playgrounds; erecting a replacement middle school and classroom and other additions; instructional technology infrastructure; and acquiring and improving sites and purchasing school buses. Debt millage is expected to be at or below 6.10 mills, a 2 mill increase from 4.10 mills levied in 2022; no series may run more than thirty (30) years; first-year millage 3.35 mills; simple average annual millage 3.94 mills. The district reports $104,165,000 of qualified bonds and $0 of qualified loans outstanding.

| 120% of average useful life | 35.72 |

Existing issues: 2014 Building & Site ($52,710,000 issued, $2,000,000 outstanding), 2015 Refunding ($31,930,000 / $12,930,000), 2016 Building & Site ($40,000,000 / $31,800,000), 2018 Building & Site ($7,125,000 / $6,610,000, limited tax), 2019 Building & Site ($27,000,000 / $19,175,000), 2020 Building & Site ($6,100,000 / $5,390,000, limited tax), 2021 Refunding Series A ($7,110,000 / $4,945,000) and Series B ($33,315,000 / $33,315,000). Proceeds of all existing bonds have not been spent.

## Bond issuance schedule

| Series | Amount | Dated | Construction fund |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | $167,000,000 | 2/1/2023 | 2/1/2023 - 5/1/2026 |
| 2 | $188,000,000 | 5/1/2026 | 5/1/2026 - 4/1/2029 |
| 3 | $200,000,000 | 5/1/2029 | 5/1/2029 - 4/1/2032 |

## Enrollment, facilities and cost

Projections were prepared by Jeff Atkins of Barton Malow Builders from the Plante Moran Cresa Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report 2022-2026, using the cohort survival method on blended Fall 2021 and Spring 2022 counts. Enrollment totals are 12,389 five years prior, 11,993 current and 11,377 projected, a change of -5.14%. Twenty-six numbered projects cover 12 elementary schools, Baker, Boulan Park and Larson middle schools, the existing and a replacement Smith Middle School, Athens and Troy high schools, International Academy, Troy College & Career High School, the Early Childhood Center and four non-instructional buildings. District square footage totals 2,294,646 with 270,584 square feet of closed facility. Combined project costs are $552,090,000 plus $7,052,105 of election and issuance costs, for $559,142,105 less $4,142,105 of estimated interest earnings.

## Document identity, certificate and professional team

Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky, rmachesky@troy.k12.mi.us, fax 248-823-4013. Program contact: Bureau of State and Authority Finance, 430 West Allegan Street, Lansing, Michigan 48922, 517-335-0994. The filing is tabbed as Certificate, Financial Summary, Enrollment Projections, Project Sheet, Building Utilization, Utilization Summary, Facility Summary and Cost Summary. The Secretary certifies that the Board, at a regular meeting noticed under Act 276 of the Public Acts of 1976 (Open Meetings Act), on the 21st day of June 2022 resolved to apply for preliminary qualification by the State Treasurer, to present the application before official action calling the election, to file a final qualification application after voter approval, approved all statements as true, and authorized the Secretary to sign and submit. Signed by Gary Hauff, Secretary; Rick West, Treasurer; Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent. Counsel reference 39235746.2/091101.00049.

## Ballot proposition

Official Ballot, Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, School Improvement Bond Proposition: borrow not to exceed Five Hundred Fifty-Five Million Dollars ($555,000,000) and issue general obligation unlimited tax bonds in one or more series for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting, completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom and other additions; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; and acquiring, preparing, developing and improving sites and purchasing school buses. Annual debt millage to retire all outstanding and proposed bonds is expected to be at or below 6.10 mills, a 2 mill increase from the 4.10 mills levied in 2022. No series may be outstanding more than thirty (30) years exclusive of refunding; estimated first-year millage 3.35 mills ($3.35 per $1,000 of taxable value); estimated simple average annual millage 3.94 mills. The district has $104,165,000 of qualified bonds and $0 of qualified loans outstanding and does not expect to borrow from the Program for debt service.

Total UTQ debt service $122,643,543 and total LT debt service $15,148,063. The"before additional bonding" millage schedule shows Debt/TV of 2.51%, a 2022 debt levy of 4.10, July levy 0%, use of funds on hand $1,472,050 and an 8.00% delinquency allowance; levy year 2022 has a projected tax base of $4,625,970,360 growing 6.77%, existing unlimited tax payments of $18,315,860 and net UT payments of $18,966,478 at 4.10 mills, declining to 0.00 mills in levy year 2034, with column totals of $122,643,543, ($1,472,050), $1,517,318, ($1,840,167) and $120,848,645. Footnotes cite $2,034,420 of equivalent IFT valuations, $0 of DDA/TIFA captures and $66,448,680 of exempt personal property for 2022; a statutory-growth variant totals $120,943,143. The PQ Millage sheets combine existing debt with the three new series at 4.00% TIC, $0 capitalized interest, a December levy cycle of 100%, Debt/TV of 6.12%, 7.80% and 9.48%, bond terms of 29 years 3 months and 30 years 0 months, average lives of 17.00, 18.16 and 18.60, and an interest factor of 0.72. Enrollment projections were prepared by Jeff Atkins of Barton Malow Builders from the Plante Moran Cresa Pupil Enrollment Projection Study Report 2022-2026, using the standard cohort survival method with blended Fall 2021 and Spring 2022 counts. ## Utilization, facility and cost summaries

The Utilization Summary reports projected five-year enrollment of 11,377 against existing pupil capacity of 10,403, new pupil capacity of 2,654 and total pupil capacity of 13,056, an 87% utilization rate, with 2,268 of closed pupil capacity; building rates range from 70% at Baker Middle School to 103% at Wass Elementary, with Athens at 79% and Troy High at 84%. The Facility Summary shows total district square footage of 2,294,646 and 270,584 square feet of closed facility, with Old Smith Middle School's 100,734 square feet marked for disposition codes 4 and 1 and Athens High School showing 0.25 acres of new site and 164,650 square feet closed. Series 1 cost summary: $89,538,544 new construction, $11,187,274 remodeling, $12,398,606 contingency, $5,341,272 instructional technology, $1,531,052 loose furnishings, $3,927,742 buses, $18,406,341 site work, $578,813 site acquisition, $9,382,445 A/E fees, $13,916,911 CM fees, $166,209,000 project costs, $2,133,792 election and issuance costs, $168,342,792 total. Series 2 totals $186,979,000 in project costs and $189,356,410 all-in; Series 3 totals $198,902,000 and $201,442,903. Combined Series 1-3: $100,384,101 new construction, $217,305,222 remodeling, $41,444,373 contingency, $21,830,509 instructional technology, $22,565,430 loose furnishings and equipment, $12,000,000 buses, $60,721,945 site work, $578,813 site acquisition, $31,248,101 A/E fees, $44,011,507 CM fees, $552,090,000 project costs and $7,052,105 election and issuance costs, for $559,142,105 less $4,142,105 of estimated interest earnings and a $555,000,000 proposed issue. Useful-life worksheets put 120% of average useful life at 44.36 for Series 1, 33.90 for Series 2, 31.10 for Series 3 and 35.72 combined, the combined sheet showing $409,638,873 of expenditures plus $62,959,894 of allocated professional fees for $472,598,767 and a weighted figure of 29.77.
